summary: World tiles show a ~0.5 px seam between tiles
author: pm
body:
The user sees a very slight gap, about 0.5 px, between world tiles in game (reported 2026-11-24). Not yet known: when it started (the folder loader 7d0a05dd, the uncommitted panel-kit renderer work under HH-0060, or older); whether it depends on window size, stretch or letterbox, smoothing settings or camera position.

**Done when:** the cause is found and fixed, and tiles meet with no seam at 800x600, 1440x1080 and fullscreen letterbox and stretch, with smoothing on and off (screenshots at 4x zoom).

Source: user report, 2026-11-24.

## Investigation (read-only, 2026-11-24)

**Cause: the Debug-only Tile Grid overlay is switched on in the user's settings.** `game/client/settings.json` has `"display": { "tileGrid": true }`. In a Debug client (the deployed DEV build is Debug), `Screen_OnGame::draw_tile_grid()` (`sources/client/screen_on_game.cpp:1159-1182`, called at `screen_on_game.cpp:737` right after `draw_background`) draws a 1 px line in (40,40,40) at 18% alpha (`GRID_ALPHA = 0.18f`, line 1168) on every tile boundary, both axes (lines 1175-1180: `x = -m_sModX + 16`, step 32). The lines move with the camera and sit exactly on the tile seams, so on open ground they look like a faint, sub-pixel gap between tiles. The toggle is System Menu > Graphics > "Tile Grid" (`dialog_box_sys_menu.cpp:602-611`, `1285-1295`). It's the last row in the Graphics list, so it only appears after scrolling the list.

**Evidence (verified, measured):** Debug client on port 8893, window 800x600 (so the world target composites 1:1 and the capture is the 800x600 world render target), Antialias Buffer off, Beginner Zone (127,70). Two captures at the same position, one with Tile Grid On and one with it Off, strip 0,380 800x160 of open grass and stone:
- Pixel diff: 7,964 px differ; 3,726 of them are at x mod 32 = 31 and 3,597 at y mod 32 = 0. The rest are the animated player and cursor. On those pixels the grid-on frame is 0.922x as bright (median), so about 8% darker.
- Column/row mean luminance minus neighbours: grid on = -8.4 (x%32=31), -6.0 (y%32=0), and 40%/38% of pixels on those lines are darker than both neighbours (median phase 21%/20%). Grid off: no phase stands out (largest -1.3, dark-ratio 0.24 vs 0.21 median).
- Seam width: one window pixel at 800x600 (one logical pixel), drawn at 18% opacity. That's why it reads as roughly half a pixel of gap rather than a solid line.
- Files: `build/screenshots/hh0070_strip_grid_on.png`, `hh0070_strip_grid_off.png` (lossless, measured region), `hh0070_zoom4x_grid_on.png`, `hh0070_zoom4x_grid_off.png` (crop 64,400 128x96 at 4x nearest). Scripts: `.claude/scratch/hh0070/seam_scan.py`, `pair_diff.py`, `alpha_scan.py`.

**Ruled out:**
- Tile drawing has integer positions (`screen_on_game_draw_objects.cpp:840-852`, `ix - 16`, `iy - 16`; camera snapped to int in `screen_on_game.cpp:692-710`). The world view is exactly 800x600 at 1:1 (`sfml_renderer.cpp:170`, in-world branch of `apply_target_view`), the sprite textures are nearest (`sfml_sprite.cpp:110`), and the draw uses an integer IntRect with an integer `setPosition` (`sfml_sprite.cpp:299-305`).
- Tile art: the manifest frames are 32x32 with pivot 0 (`maptiles1`: 9,600/9,600 frames). Ground-tile sheets are fully opaque (`maptiles1` 0-5 and 8-31, `maptiles2`, `tile406-421`). Only empty filler sheets (`maptiles1` 6/7/9) and object sheets carry alpha. There's no colour-key edge.
- Folder loader 7d0a05dd: the image bytes were verified byte-identical to the pak payloads, `load_texture()` still does `setSmooth(false)`, and the frame rects come from the same data. Same texture state, rects and padding as the old pak path.
- Uncommitted HH-0060 renderer edits (`git diff`): they touch only `create_texture_from_file` / `draw_texture_region` (filter option, tint, additive) and the `SFMLTexture(image, smooth)` constructor. Sprites and tiles never use that path.
- Upscale: at 800x600 the composite is 1:1 and the line is already in the world target.

**Regression?** No. The overlay was added in 9eedb5e8 (2026-02-05, "Add patching mode selector and grid overlays") with the 0.18 alpha line. It shows whenever the Debug client runs with `tileGrid: true`. A Release build compiles it out.

**Proposed fix:**
1. Immediate, no code: turn System Menu > Graphics > Tile Grid Off (scroll the Graphics list to the bottom).
2. Code (optional, the user's call): keep the debug overlay from being mistaken for a bug. Either (a) don't persist `tileGrid`, so it resets to off each launch (`config_manager.cpp:242-244` load, `:362` save), or (b) make it unmistakable when on (brighter colour, or a "TILE GRID" HUD tag, `screen_on_game.cpp:1166-1180`). Files: `sources/client/config_manager.cpp` and/or `sources/client/screen_on_game.cpp`. No overlap with the HH-0060 panel-kit renderer files.

Not tested: other window sizes, letterbox/stretch, Antialias Buffer on. With the cause confirmed at 1:1 these weren't needed.

Settings: `game/client/settings.json` was backed up and restored byte-for-byte (SHA-256 316F5A7B... matches). The test client (PID 41140) was stopped by PID.

**Closed, 2026-11-24:** not a bug. It was the Debug-only Tile Grid overlay, left on in settings.json. The user: "We can close it - i didn't realize it was on and I only saw it during the agent's testing/client usage". No code change.
